evidence: lifecycle_contract_covers_all_seven_operations + vc_201_042_* (8 tests, crates/susi-vendor-models/src/tests/vc_201_042.rs): one contract (crates/susi-vendor-models/src/runtime_lifecycle.rs) now spans all seven ops - Runtime::{discover,load,ready,infer,cancel,unload,health} over a RuntimeBackend trait; unsupported cancel/unload return typed EaiError via Capabilities; readiness is only a health-probe answer - process presence cannot reach Ready, and a failed probe marks Unhealthy but stays re-probeable. Production reachability: local_ecosystem::scan drives every detected HTTP-managed runtime (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp server, sglang, localai, jan, gpt4all, koboldcpp, text-generation-webui) through Runtime::discover + Runtime::health via DaemonBackend (crates/susi-vendor-models/src/local_ecosystem.rs:284-330), and scan is called from susi-daemon::discovery_pipeline (crates/susi-daemon/src/discovery_pipeline.rs:107) - so `running` is a contract health answer, not a bare port check.
missing: the native side of 'supported native and HTTP-managed runtimes': NativeInferenceEngine impls (LlamaCppEngine, SusiGgufEngine, SusiFederatedEngine in crates/susi-gemi/src/engines/runtime_native.rs) and InferenceHost (runtime_substrate.rs) do not implement or drive the RuntimeBackend contract, so no native runtime is exercised through discover/load/ready/infer/cancel/unload/health in production - only HTTP-managed daemons are, and only their discover/health verbs.
